description: Character and discipline tracking system for draft evaluation. Tracks college discipline events (academic, team rules, substance abuse, conduct, legal) and assigns character grades (exemplary, clean, concern, red_flag) that impact draft position.

discipline_events.note: Random discipline events occur during college years with 2% base chance per player per year. Events are weighted by type and result in games suspended. Hype impact directly affects player's hype stat (0-100 scale, 50 neutral). Halflife controls how quickly the impact fades from public memory.

types.description: Academic violations: GPA issues, missed classes, academic dishonesty
Team policy violations: curfew, dress code, missed meetings
Substance policy violations: failed drug tests, alcohol violations, PED suspensions
Conduct violations: unsportsmanlike behavior, altercations, code of conduct breaches
Legal issues: arrests, criminal charges, DUI, assault

team_tolerance_levels.note: Different teams have different tolerance for character concerns. This affects how they evaluate players in the draft.

strict.description: Character is paramount. Teams like the Patriots historically avoid character risks.

moderate.description: Normal evaluation. Character matters but talent can outweigh concerns.

lenient.description: Talent over character. Willing to take calculated risks on talented players.

win_now.description: Desperate for talent. Will draft anyone who can help immediately.

character_grades.note: Character grades are evaluated at draft time based on complete discipline history. Draft impact flows through the hype stat which is modified when events occur.

exemplary.description: No discipline issues throughout college career. Player maintains baseline hype unaffected by character concerns.

clean.description: Single minor incident only. Minimal hype impact - considered normal college behavior.

concern.description: Multiple minor incidents or single moderate incident. Cumulative hype impact affects draft perception.

red_flag.description: Serious character concerns: legal trouble, multiple major incidents, or pattern of behavior. Significant negative hype impact affects draft stock substantially.

interview_red_flags.note: PHASE 2 FEATURE - Currently disabled. Will simulate pre-draft visits and interviews where scouts can detect hidden character concerns.
interview_red_flags.description: When enabled, scouts conduct pre-draft interviews. Higher scout skill increases red flag detection chance. Detected flags amplify character grade penalties.

draft_integration.note: Character events directly modify the player's hype stat. Draft evaluation uses hype through CollegeAwardsService mock draft rankings.
draft_integration.description: Character events immediately affect hype when they occur. The cumulative hype change flows into draft evaluation through the existing hype → mock draft → draft stock pipeline.

player_history.note: All discipline events are logged to player.history array alongside awards and other career milestones.

event_format.year: int - college year when event occurred
event_format.hype_impact: float - change applied to hype stat

tuning_notes.base_chance_rationale: 2% per year means ~8% of draft class has discipline history (32 out of 400 players). Matches real NFL draft data where 5-10% of prospects have character concerns.
tuning_notes.weight_distribution_rationale: Academic (40%) and team rules (30%) are most common but least impactful. Legal trouble (5%) is rare but creates red flags. Distribution matches NCAA violation statistics.
tuning_notes.grade_distribution_expected: Exemplary: 65%, Clean: 20%, Concern: 12%, Red Flag: 3%. Most players have clean records, serious concerns are rare.
tuning_notes.hype_impact_rationale: Hype impacts scaled to 0-100 hype range. Minor events (-2 to -3) barely noticeable. Legal trouble (-35) can devastate draft stock. Multiple events compound.
tuning_notes.halflife_rationale: Minor violations fade quickly (0.25-0.5 years) as media moves on. Serious incidents linger longer (1-1.5 years) but still decay. This allows players to rehabilitate their image over time. A legal issue at start of junior year (-35 hype) decays to ~-17.5 by draft day (1 year later).
tuning_notes.team_tolerance_rationale: Real NFL teams vary significantly in character evaluation. Patriots historically strict, Raiders historically lenient. Win-now teams desperate for talent may overlook red flags. Tolerance affects draft position variance - same player might go round 1 to one team, round 3 to another.

examples.randy_gregory: Multiple substance abuse issues would accumulate -30+ hype over time, but with 0.75 year halflife some recovery is possible between incidents.
examples.laremy_tunsil: Single major incident (conduct -20) right before draft with no time to decay. Team tolerance determines if he's a first-round pick or falls to day 2.
